children: , the largest U.S. bank by assets, gained a clearer view of how the Federal Reserve plans to reshape its annual stress tests. Shares slipped approximately 0.7% to $346.91 Friday morning. The Fed's overhaul is designed to make the process more transparent and predictable, with final changes expected within weeks.

Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said the central bank plans to disclose more detail about the models, variables and economic scenarios behind the tests. The Fed also intends to average each bank's two most recent stress-test results when setting its stress capital buffer, rather than letting a single annual result carry all the weight. For JPMorgan, that could smooth swings in required capital from one year to the next, although the new framework does not automatically mean a lower requirement.

The bigger investor takeaway is predictability. A less volatile capital buffer could give JPMorgan more visibility when planning dividends and buybacks, even though a weak test result may now linger across two calculation cycles. The valuation picture adds another wrinkle: the shares at $346.91 sit 9.22% above the $317.62 GF Value estimate shown in the chart. That premium suggests investors are already paying above GuruFocus' modeled fair-value level while waiting to see whether the Fed's changes translate into steadier capital planning.

title: JPMorgan Slips as Fed Smooths Stress-Capital Volatility
